title: He Still Moves Stones: Everyone Needs a Miracle
author: Max Lucado
target_audience: Christians seeking encouragement and faith-building content
Individuals facing difficult life circumstances or feeling hopeless
Readers interested in biblical miracles and their relevance today
Anyone exploring the power of faith and God's intervention
core_themes: Miracles in the life and ministry of Jesus
God’s ongoing involvement in people’s lives
Hope in the midst of hardship
God’s compassion and presence in suffering
primary_purpose: To reassure and inspire readers by illustrating that the miraculous works of Jesus in the Bible are still possible today, and to encourage faith that God continues to intervene lovingly and powerfully in everyday lives.

structure_format.narrative_style: Conversational, empathetic, and story-driven, with pastoral encouragement
structure_format.organization: Organized around gospel narratives of Jesus’ miracles, each chapter focusing on a different story or miracle
features: Retelling of biblical stories with modern application
Accessible language to reach a broad readership

key_concepts_lessons: The miracles of Jesus are not relics of the past, but evidence of God’s character and concern for people today.
Difficulties and suffering are opportunities for God to demonstrate His love and power.
Faith, even amid doubt or struggle, positions individuals to receive help and hope.
God meets people in their brokenness, responding compassionately to their needs.
Everyone faces ‘stones’—obstacles they cannot move on their own—but God specializes in doing the impossible.
notable_features: Blends Bible narrative with modern-day relevance
Focuses on emotional and spiritual encouragement
Relatable storytelling and practical faith application
Frequently used in church small groups and counseling
cultural_historical_context: Published in the early 1990s during a growing popularity of devotional and inspirational Christian literature, the book provides reassurance to readers wrestling with adversity, echoing the evangelical Christian message of hope, faith, and divine intervention.
reception_impact: Well-loved among Christian readers and church groups for its uplifting message
Frequently cited as offering comfort in times of crises or loss
Praised for Lucado’s accessible writing and heartfelt storytelling
Used as a resource for teaching and personal devotion in evangelical circles
comparable_titles: Just Like Jesus by Max Lucado
Jesus: A Pilgrimage by James Martin
The Case for Miracles by Lee Strobel
